mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyAuditEntries allows the model to produce two AuditEntries for the same application that record the same (prevStatus, newStatus) — exactly an in-place update of a prior entry. The injection forces this violated instance to exist so AppendOnly and FR_018_AuditImmutable both find counterexamples.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.application = ae2.application and ae1.prevStatus = ae2.prevStatus and ae1.newStatus = ae2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_NoSelfApproval allows an officer to decide their own application. The injection forces an AuditEntry whose actor is the same User as the application's applicant and has a non-null prevStatus, directly violating the no-self-approval invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfApprovalViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | some ae.prevStatus and ae.actor = ae.application.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_RoleMultiplicity allows a User to simultaneously hold Officer and Auditor roles, violating the mutual-exclusion invariant from FR-002 and the data-model CHECK constraint.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_RoleMultiplicityViolation { some u: User | Officer in u.roles and Auditor in u.roles }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OnlyAssignedOfficerTransitions allows a non-assigned officer to author a transition AuditEntry, violating FR-012 and AttributionCorrectness. The injection forces a non-initial entry whose actor is different from the application's assignedOfficer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnassignedOfficerTransition { some ae: AuditEntry | some ae.prevStatus and ae.actor != ae.application.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_PermissionMatrix frees the Allowed relation to include forbidden cells such as Auditor->PatchApplicationStatus or Applicant->GetApplicationAudit. The injection adds the most dangerous forbidden cell, letting LeastPrivilege and FR_005_AuditorReadOnly find counterexamples.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { Auditor -> PatchApplicationStatus in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_OneInFlightPerApplicant allows the same applicant to have two LoanApplications simultaneously in the Pending or UnderReview state. The injection forces this duplicate in-flight situation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateInFlight { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.applicant = a2.applicant and a1.status in (Pending + UnderReview) and a2.status in (Pending + UnderReview) }
